THE YMCA YEAR BOOK IS READABLE FROM HERE — EVERY YEAR THIS PROJECT CALLED MISSING
==================================================================================
Compiled 2026-09-07. THIS FILE SUPERSEDES THE ACCESS-FAILURE VERDICT IN
2026-09-06-hathitrust-holdings-the-missing-years.txt AND THE CLOSING PARAGRAPH OF
2026-09-06-complete-ia-inventory-of-the-series.txt. Both remain accurate about the Internet
Archive and about HathiTrust. Both were wrong about the conclusion drawn from them, which was
that this environment cannot read the missing years. It can.

WHAT WAS WRONG WITH YESTERDAY'S VERDICT
---------------------------------------
Yesterday's note listed four routes to the 1901-1905 and 1910-1920 volumes and found three shut
(HathiTrust behind Cloudflare, Google Books behind a quota, the Data API behind OAuth). The
fourth was written down as "the Kautz Family YMCA Archives, University of Minnesota, WHICH HOLDS
THE SERIES IN PRINT." That last clause was an assumption, not a finding. Nobody had asked
Minnesota whether it also holds the series digitally. It does, and the digital copy is open.

Retried first, for the record, because the note said to: Google Books still returns HTTP 429,
and the quota message names THE SAME consumer project number as yesterday. That reframes it —
it is a shared key exhausted by other traffic, not a daily allowance that resets for this
session, so "retry tomorrow" is not the fix. books.google.com and google.com/search?tbm=bks both
302 to /sorry/index, Google's bot wall. babel.hathitrust.org is still the Cloudflare
interstitial. So three of yesterday's four routes are shut today as well; only the untested
assumption gave way.

THE ROUTE THAT WORKS
--------------------
University of Minnesota Libraries, collection "YMCA Yearbooks, Directories, and Proceedings",
ContentDM alias p16022coll351 on cdm16022.contentdm.oclc.org. 173 items. Finding aid:
https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/7/resources/883

Two endpoints, both answering normally from this environment:

  ENUMERATE / FULL-TEXT SEARCH
  https://cdm16022.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/bl/dmwebservices/index.php?q=
      dmQuery/p16022coll351/<searchstring>/title!dmrecord/nosort/<rows>/<start>/0/0/0/json
  searchstring is either 0 (everything) or FIELD^TERMS^MODE^OPERATOR, e.g.
      CISOSEARCHALL^Kanawana^all^and          (all words)
      CISOSEARCHALL^Harold C. Cross^exact^and (exact phrase — verified working)
  Hits come back AT PAGE LEVEL, each carrying parentobject = the volume's dmrecord.

  READ ONE PAGE'S OCR
  ...index.php?q=dmGetItemInfo/p16022coll351/<page dmrecord>/json
  The OCR is the "transc" field. NOTE: cdmhasocr reads 0 on pages that plainly have OCR in
  transc, so DO NOT USE cdmhasocr TO DECIDE WHETHER A PAGE IS READABLE. Read transc.

  UMedia's own search.json (umedia.lib.umn.edu) also answers but IGNORES the set_spec and
  facets parameters — it returned Social Work Year Books and county maps for collection-scoped
  queries. Use ContentDM directly.

EVERY HOLE IS HERE, WITH ITS RECORD NUMBER
------------------------------------------
The years the Internet Archive lacks entirely, and the three HathiTrust also lacks (starred):

  1883        2255        1909-10     11112
  1901        13624       1910-11     5935
  1902        13285       1911-12     9872
  1902-03     14318       1912-13 *   5467
  1903-04     14699       1913-14     5052
  1904-05     1059        1914-15 *   6336
  1905-06     8010        1915-16     9113
                          1916-17     3985
                          1917-18     15936
                          1918-19     15358
                          1919-20     16539
                          1920-21 *   34602

The collection also runs forward through 1982 (the 1957-1968 volumes are what carry Kanawana;
see below), and holds 1885 and 1889 — the remaining two nineteenth-century holes — is NOT
established here and was not checked.

OCR COVERAGE WAS CONTROLLED BEFORE ANY NULL WAS TRUSTED
-------------------------------------------------------
A full-text search for "Montreal" returns 2,742 page hits across 124 distinct volumes, and
EVERY ONE of the nineteen target volumes above appears among them. So these volumes are OCR'd
and searchable, and a null in them is a null in the book rather than a hole in the scanning.
That control is what makes the two nulls recorded below worth anything.


FINDING 1 — "KANAWANA" APPEARS IN THIS SERIES ONLY FROM 1957 TO 1968
=====================================================================
Seventeen pages, in eleven volumes: 1957, 1958, 1959, 1960, 1961, 1963, 1964, 1965, 1966, 1967,
1968. Not once before 1957 and not once after 1968, across a series running 1877-1982.

THAT IS A NULL ABOUT THE NATIONAL ROSTER, NOT ABOUT THE CAMP. What changes in the late 1950s is
almost certainly the roster's own practice — camps start being listed as posts within a
metropolitan board — not anything about Kanawana, which had been running for sixty years by
then. Do not read the 1894-1956 silence as evidence of anything except that this particular
publication did not name camps.

The camp is spelled "Kamp Kanawana" in the roster from 1957 through 1965 and "Camp Kanawana"
from 1966. This project already knows the K spelling well; it is recorded here only because the
changeover year is clean in this series.

THE DIRECTOR SERIES, VERBATIM FROM THE QUEBEC BLOCK OF THE DIRECTORY OF ASSOCIATIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1957  "Assistant Program, Kamp Kanawana, Murray B. Shantz"      (Montreal Metro. Bd.)
1958  "Assistant Program, Kamp Kanawana, Murray B. Shantz"
1959  "Assistant Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1960  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1961  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1963  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1964  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1965  "Program, Kamp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1966  "Program, Camp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1967  "Program, Camp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"
1968  "Program, Camp Kanawana, A. Ross Seaman"

1962 IS ABSENT FROM THE HIT LIST and it is not clear whether the 1962 volume is in this
collection at all — that was not checked. Do not record 1962 as a null until it is.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE WIKI, PRECISELY
  - directors-index.md carries Shantz at 1955-1958 with "1956-1958 is inference from that
    silence" — inference from the Montreal annual reports NOT recording a change. The 1957 and
    1958 Year Books state him in the post outright, from outside Montreal's own paper. Two of
    those three inferred years become documented.
  - The same index says of 1968: "Summer 1968 has no named on-site director anywhere — not in
    the annual report, not in any 1968 news release or newsletter." The 1968 Year Book names
    Seaman in the Kanawana post. READ IT CAREFULLY BEFORE CLAIMING TOO MUCH: this is the
    Metropolitan Board's staff roster and gives him the camp, exactly as it does for 1966 and
    1967; it does not use the words "on-site director," and the index's own warning about the
    branch-officers table — that the man holding the camping portfolio is not always the man on
    site — applies here with equal force. What it establishes is that a national publication
    put Seaman in the Kanawana post for 1968. It does not establish who ran the 1968 season on
    the ground.
  - Seaman's own entry line in the alphabetical list of employed officers gives his year of
    entry into Association work as 53, and the 1957 and 1958 volumes place him at "Montreal,
    Que., Lachine, Exec" — Executive of the Lachine YMCA in the two years before he took the
    camp. The index says only "career in community work preceded directorship."
  - Shantz's entry line gives his year of entry as 46, and the 1959 and later volumes show him
    at "Toronto, Ont., Sec. National Council" — corroborating the index's "left in 1959 for the
    YMCA National Council staff" from an independent source.
  - Camp Otoreke: "Dir. Camp Otoreke, Clarence J. McGerrigle" 1957-1961, and "Program, Camp
    Otoreke, Colin R. McKay" 1963-1965. COLIN R. McKAY OCCURS NOWHERE IN THIS PROJECT — checked
    by grep across wiki, kb, project-docs and the source index before writing this line.


FINDING 2 — W. J. HOLLIDAY DID NOT GET THE BOYS' WORK DIRECTORSHIP BACK
========================================================================
This was question 1 on yesterday's list, and the answer is no. He goes sideways into branch
administration and stays there for at least seven years.

  1909-10  Montreal, Central Dept.: "Asst., (Memb.,) W. J. Holliday" — a membership assistant.
  1910-11  "Fairmount Ave. Br., Ch., W. A. Wilson / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1911-12  "North Br., Chairman, W. A. Wilson / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1912-13  "North Br. ... Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1913-14  "North Br., Chairman, H. R. MacGregor / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1914-15  "North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Chairman, George S. Rorke / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1915-16  "North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Chairman, George S. Rorke / Secy., W. J. Holliday"
  1916-17  "North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Chairman, S. W. Cuthbert / Secy., W. J. Holliday"

The Fairmount Avenue branch of 1910-11 and the North Branch of 1911 onward share a chairman
(W. A. Wilson) and a secretary (Holliday) across the changeover, which suggests the same branch
under a new name at 2300 Park Ave. THAT IS AN INFERENCE FROM TWO NAMES AND IS NOT STATED
ANYWHERE IN THESE VOLUMES.

AND THE MONTREAL BOYS' WORK POST ITSELF, YEAR BY YEAR — yesterday's question 2, the closest
thing to a list of the men over the camp through the new site's first decade:

  1910-11  Central Dept., "Boys, Kenneth J. Hollinshead"
  1911-12  Central Dept., "Boys, Kenneth J. Hollinshead"
  1912-13  Central Dept., "Boys, D. J. Evans" (with "Asst. Boys, H. A. Lordly")
  1913-14  Central Dept., "Boys, D. J. Evans"
  1914-15  Central Br., "Boys," — THE LINE IS PRINTED WITH NO NAME AFTER IT
  1915-16  Central Br., "Boys, John G. MacKinnon"
  1916-17  Central Br., "Boys, John G. MacKinnon"

KENNETH J. HOLLINSHEAD OCCURS NOWHERE IN THIS PROJECT; so does no Percy D. Brandon and no
Arthur L. Walsh. All three checked by grep before writing.

A CAUTION THAT MATTERS FOR THE CAMP. These are the CENTRAL DEPARTMENT / CENTRAL BRANCH boys'
workers. The 1909-10 volume prints "Boys' Work Dir." as a separate line from the branch "Boys"
lines, which means the association-level directorship and a branch boys' post are not the same
office. Whether the man who ran Kanawana in these years is the Central Branch's boys' worker,
an association-level Boys' Work Director, or someone the Year Book does not list at all is NOT
settled by any of the above. What is settled is that Holliday was not it.


FINDING 3 — WHERE HAROLD C. CROSS WAS BETWEEN 1912 AND 1919
============================================================
wiki/people/harold-cross.md states the question in those words: his 1921 entry-year figure of
"12" is "seven years earlier than any date this article had, and it opens a question that did
not exist before: where was he between 1912 and 1919?" Five of those years now have an answer,
and the first three of them say Montreal.

  1911-12  "North Br. ... Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"      MONTREAL
  1912-13  "North Br. ... Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"      MONTREAL
  1913-14  "North Br. ... Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"      MONTREAL
  1914-15  "Prince Edward Island / Charlottetown ... Gen. Secy., Harold C. Cross"
  1915-16  Charlottetown's General Secretary is J. Morrison Clark. Cross is gone.
  1915-16, 1916-17, 1917-18  ABSENT — an exact-phrase search for "Harold C. Cross" returns no
           page in any of these three volumes, which ARE OCR'd (see the control above).
  1918-19  "Victoria. President, / Gen. Secy., J. M. Graham / Asst., Harry H. Hollins /
            Physical, James Thompson / Boys, Harold C. Cross"                   VICTORIA, B.C.
  1920-21  "Victoria. President, George McGregor / Gen. Secy., J. M. Graham / ...
            Physical, W. S. Maguire / Boys, Harold C. Cross"                    VICTORIA, B.C.

SO: a Montreal YMCA boys' worker at the North Branch for three years in the early 1910s, more
than a decade before he directed Kanawana; then General Secretary at Charlottetown for a year;
then unfound for three volumes; then Boys' Work at Victoria, where the article already had him
from 1919 on a Concordia source. The Victoria years are now corroborated from outside Concordia.

TWO THINGS TO HOLD LOOSELY HERE.
1. The three absent volumes are a null in this series, not a finding about his whereabouts.
   The obvious guess is war service and the obvious check is a CEF service file, but this
   document does not support the guess and it is not recorded as a fact.
2. The entry-year figure of "12" printed in 1921 sits a year later than his first appearance
   in the 1911-12 volume. Either the volume year and the roster year overlap, or the figure is
   approximate. Not resolved; noted so nobody later reads a contradiction into it.

AND ONE HUMAN DETAIL THAT IS DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN INFERRED: W. S. MAGUIRE is the Physical
Director alongside Cross at Montreal's North Branch through 1911-1916, is General Secretary at
Brandon, Manitoba in 1918-19, and is Physical Director at VICTORIA alongside Cross again in
1920-21. The two men appear on the same branch staff on opposite coasts nine years apart.


A THIRD NAME FOR THE CUSHING TANGLE
-----------------------------------
"Central Br., 127 Drummond St., Chairman, LEMUEL CUSHING" in both 1914-15 and 1915-16. This
project already has a Lemuel Cushing taking boys to Lake Saint-Joseph in 1892 and a W. E.
Cushing on the 1892 committee, and yesterday's inventory added a Charles Cushing as the YMCA's
corresponding member for Quebec in 1887. A Lemuel Cushing chairing Montreal's Central Branch
twenty-two years after the Lake Saint-Joseph trip is either the same man late in life or a
younger relative. NEITHER IS ESTABLISHED HERE. It is a name, a post and two years.


QUERIES RUN
-----------
googleapis.com/books/v1/volumes with a control (429, same consumer project as yesterday);
books.google.com and google.com/search?tbm=bks (302 to /sorry/); babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt
(403 Cloudflare); umedia.lib.umn.edu/search.json bare, with set_spec, and with facets[] forms;
archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/14/resources (202, empty body);
dmQuery on p16022coll351 for: everything (173), CISOSEARCHALL Kanawana (17 pages, 11 volumes),
Montreal (2,742 pages, 124 volumes — the OCR control), Holliday (243), Jubilee (112),
"Holliday Montreal Boys" (67), and exact-phrase "Harold C. Cross" (39);
dmGetItemInfo on page records 40653, 10775, 5588, 9511, 5075, 4630, 6211, 8974, 3834, 34456,
15084, 34016 and the seventeen Kanawana pages.


==========================================================================================
SECOND PASS, THE SAME DAY — THE 1900-1906 MONTREAL BLOCK, AND WHAT 1962 ACTUALLY SAYS
==========================================================================================

W. H. BALL'S DEPARTURE, NARROWED FROM FIVE YEARS TO ONE BOUNDARY
  1900     "Montreal ... Phys. Director, W. H. Ball, Jr."
  1901     "Phys.Director. W. H Ball, Jr. / Asst. Phys. Dir., Arthur B. Dawson"
  1902     "Phys. Director. J. E. Merritt / Asst. Phys. Dir., Arthur B. Dawson"
Merritt succeeded Ball directly at the 1901/1902 boundary; the assistant stayed through it.

THE TRAP, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY WORKED. An exact-phrase search for "W. H. Ball" returns
44 pages across the series, and the hits in the 1902, 1904-05, 1905-06 and 1906-07 volumes are
THREE OTHER MEN: a W. H. Ball at Brooklyn's Prospect Park Branch, one at Springfield,
Massachusetts, and one who is DETROIT's Physical Director for at least two years. Following the
name would have kept Montreal's Ball in post until 1907 and been wrong by six years. The answer
came from reading Montreal's own block in each volume. A related hazard on the same pages:
Montreal's assistant physical director in 1902-03 and 1903-04 is HAROLD G. BEALL.

FINDING THE MONTREAL BLOCK AT ALL IS THE FIDDLY PART. Each volume prints the same men twice —
an international-committee membership list and the Directory of Associations — and a search for
"D. A. Budge" returns both. The committee list is the one that runs "D. A. Budge ... Montreal,
Que. / G. H. Harrower / A. Kingman / L. H. Packard"; the directory is the one that runs
"Montreal ... Pres. / Gen. Secy. / Asst. / Phys. Director". Searching for "J. E. Merritt"
lands on the directory page directly and is the faster route.

THE MONTREAL BOYS' WORK LINE, WHICH IS THE OFFICE THAT RAN THE CAMP
  1900        "Junior Dept.,"          NO NAME PRINTED
  1901, 1902  "Boys' Dept., John Brown"
  1902-03     "Boys' Secy,"            NO NAME PRINTED
  1903-04     "Boys' Work Director, Cecil M. Daggett"
  1904-05     "Boys' Work Dir.,"       NO NAME PRINTED
  1905-06     "Boys' Work Dir., W. A. Maclaren"
CECIL M. DAGGETT occurs nowhere else in this project. A blank line is NOT a vacant office —
these rosters leave lines blank routinely, Montreal's Educational Director among them.

AND A CORRECTION TO THIS PROJECT'S OWN TRANSCRIPTION. f_4967 quotes the 1906 Montreal block as
ending "Phys. Dir., J. E. MERRITT. Asst. Phys. Dir., William Sovereign." The Minnesota scan of
the same volume gives the identical list and then ONE MORE LINE, which is the last on the page:
"Boys' Work Dir., W. A. Maclaren". So 1906's boys' work post was filled, and Holliday — listed
that year as a plain assistant — was the junior man under Maclaren rather than a man appearing
from nowhere in 1907. The two then trade places twice: Holliday takes boys' work in 1907-08;
by 1909 he is an assistant again and MACLAREN is secretary of the Fairmount Avenue Branch; and
by 1910-11 HOLLIDAY is secretary of the Fairmount Avenue Branch. Entry years: Maclaren 04,
Holliday 06.

WHY 1962 RETURNED NO "KANAWANA" HIT
The 1962 volume IS in the collection (record 34925) and IS searchable — it returns "Kamp" (in
"Kamp Kiamesha", a New Jersey camp), "Otoreke" and "Hubbard". Its Quebec block reads:
"... Staff Training & Development, Hedley G. Dimock / PROGRAM, A. ROSS SEAMAN / Public
Relations, Gerald H. Wright / Director Camp Otoreke, Clarence J. McGerrigle."
SEAMAN IS THERE, in the same slot he holds in 1961 and 1963. The roster prints his title as bare
"Program" that year and drops the camp's name, while Otoreke's line on the very next row keeps
its own. The null is one word in one year; the 1959-1968 run is unbroken.

The 1962 employed-officers list also gives "McKay, C. R., Kitchener, Ont., Adult Program, 52" —
Colin R. McKay at Kitchener the year before he turns up at Montreal running Otoreke — and
"McGerrigle, C. J., Montreal, Que., Met. Bd., Dir. Camp Otoreke, 27".

STILL UNCHECKED: the 1885 (record 11848) and 1889 (13974) volumes, both in the collection, both
unread. They are the last two nineteenth-century holes in this series.


==========================================================================================
THIRD PASS — THE WAR YEARS' MONTREAL BLOCK, WHICH THE FIRST PASS DID NOT REACH
==========================================================================================

THE ONE THAT MATTERS: THE CAMP'S DIRECTOR AND CENTRAL'S BOYS' WORKER ARE THE SAME MAN, 1916-1919
  Year Book, Central Br., Boys:  John G. MacKinnon in 1915-16, 1916-17, 1917-18 and 1918-19.
  Annual reports (already held): MacKinnon directs Kanawana in 1916, 1917, 1918 (to 3 August)
                                 and 1919 -- "Mr. MacKinnon has been appointed Director for
                                 this season."
Two publications with no view of each other, one man, the same four years. By the 1920-21
volume the post has passed to R. E. G. Davis and MacKinnon is Industrial Secretary.
THIS QUALIFIES THE CAUTION WRITTEN IN THE FIRST PASS. It remains true that a branch boys' post
and an association-level Boys' Work directorship are two different offices. But for 1916-1919
the question of which one the camp answered to has an answer, and it makes the Central Branch
boys' post the first place to look for Hollinshead (1910-12) and D. J. Evans (1912-14).

HOLLIDAY VANISHES, 1917 TO 1922
  1911-12 to 1916-17   North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Secy., W. J. Holliday
  1917-18              North Br., Secy., THOMAS S. SMITH   -- Holliday not in the Montreal block
  1918-19              North Br., Secy., Thomas S. Smith   -- Holliday not in the Montreal block
  1922 (already held)  North Br., 2300 Park Ave., Secy., W. J. Holliday
A five-year hole in the middle of the career of the man the 1931 report calls the camp's first
director, opening in the last year of the war. IT IS A NULL IN ONE PUBLICATION. The far end is
soft: the 1919-20 and 1920-21 volumes were read at their North Branch and Westmount blocks, not
swept whole for the name.

NORTH BRANCH BOYS' WORKERS AFTER CROSS
  1914-15, 1915-16   Arthur L. Walsh
  1916-17            S. Burton Cuthbert
  1917-18, 1918-19   J. G. Cruickshank
  1919-20            Charles G. Hewett
  1920-21            Geoffrey Guiton, with Robert E. Blake and G. S. Mooney as assistants
Cruickshank and Hewett occur nowhere else in this project. This is Cross's branch (1911-14) and
Holliday's branch (1911-17), so the list is worth having whole; no camp connection is documented
for any of these four.

GRANT D. BRANDON, EARLIER THAN THIS PROJECT HAD HIM
  1918-19   Central Br., "Community, Grant D. Brandon"
  1920-21   association level, "Community, R. Gordon Burgoyne / Community, Grant D. Brandon"
The project's earliest sighting was the 1921 volume. He directs Kanawana in 1921, so THE 1921
CAMP DIRECTOR WAS THE ASSOCIATION'S COMMUNITY SECRETARY, not its boys' work secretary -- one
more case of the camp directorship sitting apart from the boys' work post.
KEEP APART: PERCY D. BRANDON is a different man in the same rosters -- Assistant Physical at
Central in 1915-16, Boys Physical in 1916-17 and 1917-18. Two Brandons, no established relation.

FINDING THE MONTREAL BLOCK IN THE LATER VOLUMES: an exact-phrase search for "D. A. Budge" still
works (he is Consulting Secretary into the 1920s), and "Westmount Br" is a good second probe
since the Montreal block always runs Central, North, Westmount, R. R. in that order.


==========================================================================================
FOURTH PASS — AND THIS ONE FETCHED NOTHING
==========================================================================================

Every finding below comes from YMCA of Montreal annual reports already in this project's cache,
in files marked read. The Year Book's contribution was the NAMES. Hollinshead, Lordly, Daggett
and Murray Brooks occurred nowhere in this project, so nobody could grep for them.

FROM THE 1910 ANNUAL REPORT (sgw-ymca-annual-report-1910.txt):
  "Next month Mr. K. J. HOLLINSHEAD, OF ALBION COLLEGE, MICHIGAN, will take up the Boys'
   Secretaryship, which MR. MURRAY BROOKS RESIGNED TO GO AS STRATHCONA HALL'S REPRESENTATIVE
   IN THE FOREIGN WORK IN CEYLON."
  "The Central Association will also lose, with regret, MR. HOLLIDAY'S SERVICES, AS IN THE EARLY
   FALL HE GOES AS SECRETARY TO THE FAIRMOUNT BRANCH, PREPARING THE WAY FOR THE LARGER WORK IN
   THE ANNEX, WHICH THE NEW BUILDING WILL ENTAIL."

FROM THE 1913 ANNUAL REPORT:
  "Mr. K. J. Hollinshead LEAVES ON AUGUST 1ST to take up Community Work, and will be succeeded
   by MR. D. J. EVANS, FORMERLY PROVINCIAL SECRETARY OF THE BOY SCOUTS' MOVEMENT. MR. H. A.
   LORDLY joined the Boys' Department staff in July, SUCCEEDING MR. H. W. RITTENHOUSE."

FROM THE 1914 ANNUAL REPORT (year ending 30 April 1914, so the summer of 1913):
  "The Boys' Camp at Lake Kanawana was open for July and August with 162 boys, apart from
   visitors, IN CHARGE OF MESSRS. D. J. EVANS, HAROLD CROSS, AND H. A. LORDLY FOR SUCCESSIVE
   PORTIONS OF THE SEASON."
  (The men's camp at Lake St. Joseph the same summer: H. C. Patterson, 160 men, 5 July to
   2 September.)

WHAT THAT SETTLES
  - M. G. Brooks is MURRAY BROOKS; he RESIGNED, and went to Ceylon. p_466 closed.
  - The Boys' Secretaryship: Brooks -> mid-1910 Hollinshead -> 1 Aug 1913 D. J. Evans.
  - Holliday's 1909-10 move to Fairmount was a posting to open a branch ahead of a new
    building, "with regret" — not a demotion. directors-index.md had deliberately left the
    reason open; the association supplied one.
  - HAROLD C. CROSS WAS AT KANAWANA IN 1913, twelve years before his directorship.

AND THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART, WHICH IS THE REAL LESSON
The 162-boy figure in that last quotation has been in attendance-series.md for months. It was
taken from the sentence that names three men. The number came out; the names stayed in.
A DOCUMENT MARKED "extracted" HAS BEEN READ FOR THE QUESTIONS SOMEBODY HAD AT THE TIME. That is
not the same as having been read. And the corollary is the practical rule: WHEN AN OUTSIDE
SOURCE HANDS YOU A NEW NAME FOR AN INSTITUTION THIS PROJECT ALREADY HOLDS DOCUMENTS ABOUT, GREP
THE CACHE FOR IT IMMEDIATELY, before doing anything else with it.


==========================================================================================
FIFTH PASS — THE 1885 AND 1889 VOLUMES (p_469), AND BALL AT SPRINGFIELD
==========================================================================================

1889, record 13974, page 239 (rec 13863), under "CORRESPONDING MEMBERS OF THE CONVENTION":
  "Rev. David Allen Read, Springfield, Mass. / G. D. Baker, Ass'n Train. School, [ditto] /
   WM. H. BALL, JR., [ditto] / Geo. W. Banning, [ditto] / S. E. Barrett / K. O. Bartlett /
   J. E. Canfield / F. M. Carey / A. T. Carson ..."
The ditto marks OCR as "44", "14" and "4 4". The whole run is Association Training School,
Springfield, Massachusetts.

WHY IT MATTERS: this project has Ball entering Association work in 1889 (f_4976) and Montreal
introducing him in 1892 as "the physical director, W. H. Ball Jr., A NEW MAN, FROM THE
SPRINGFIELD TRAINING SCHOOL", with 1884, 1886, 1887, 1888 and 1890 holding no W. H. Ball at all.
The 1889 volume catches him at the school in the year he entered the work. Montreal's account of
where he came from is now corroborated from OUTSIDE MONTREAL and CONTEMPORANEOUSLY.

STRONG, NOT CERTAIN. Four different W. H. Balls appear across this series (f_5273) and the
surname is common in the association. None of the others is at Springfield, and the "Jr." and
the year both match. Recorded that way.

1885 (record 11848) HOLDS NO W. H. BALL. Its only Ball is an F. D. Ball. 1890 and 1891 are still
blank and there is nothing left in this series to try for them.

FIVE MONTREAL NAMES ON THE SAME 1889 PAGE, none of them previously anywhere in this project:
  "Charles Babcock, Montreal, Que. / J. S. Hetherington / Robert S. Ross / Wm. Sloan /
   John R. Terrill" (the last OCR'd "Terrtll")
Convention volunteers, not paid officers. Grepped against the cache immediately, per the rule:
a WM. SLOAN sits on the association's EXTENSION FUND committee in the report for 1893-94, THE
CAMP'S FOUNDING YEAR, with John P. Copland under chairman Geo. H. Harrower; J. S. Hetherington
appears there only as a ten-dollar subscriber. Whether the committee's Sloan is the convention's
Sloan is NOT established, and the same report separately lists a John J. Sloan and a Geo. Sloan.
